Calibrate a declared allocation model, by default from starts found in the data

Source: R/06-ae_workflow.R
fit_allocation.Rd

Count targets and loss choice are separate. When starts are given, the loss defaults to weighted SSE; name Poisson explicitly. Custom loss/gradient functions pass through. Observation-indexed loss arguments must be in canonical order. Starts, boundaries, failed runs and disagreement retain the existing multistart result; a selected fit is not a claim of identification or global optimality.

Usage

fit_allocation(
  model,
  observed,
  starts = NULL,
  lower = NULL,
  upper = NULL,
  output = "utilization",
  loss = "weighted_sse",
  loss_args = list(),
  loss_grad = NULL,
  gradient = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

model

A static CLM from clm_allocation() or huff_allocation(). A kernel declared smooth = FALSE cannot be fitted.

observed

Numeric vector or origin-by-facility matrix. A one-dimensional array or table, such as the result of tapply() or table(), is read as the vector named by its names. For a factor level without records tapply() gives NA, which the fit reads as unobserved: give it default = 0 (or use table()) when no record means a count of zero. Named axes match declared IDs independently; unnamed axes are positional. Keep all IDs and use NA for unobserved entries. The count-valued utilization, flow, utilization_by_group and outside-count targets reject negative nonmissing observations; fractional counts are allowed. Other output domains pass to the fitter as given. For utilization_by_group (a model with demand groups) a facility-by-group matrix of observed counts with both axes named (group columns by group ID, facility rows by facility ID, any order). For the outside-count outputs the same shapes with the outside count added under the name "(outside)": for flow_outside an extra column of the origin-by-facility matrix, for utilization_outside an extra element of the named vector, for utilization_outside_by_group an extra row of the facility-by-group matrix. The names are matched to the IDs in any order, the outside entry included, and NA leaves an outside count unobserved.

starts

NULL (default) for the default search, or a finite positive matrix, one explicit independent start per row, with exactly the named model parameter columns. No random starts are added. Each start must lie inside the bounds. Given starts with lower or upper missing or partial use default bounds for the missing entries, widened to include every start.

lower, upper

NULL (default), or named positive parameter bounds with lower < upper: complete, or for some of the parameters only (the default bounds replace the missing entries). For a declared kernel, the starts and bounds of sigma must lie within the bounds of the declaration.

output

Exact model output to calibrate; default facility utilization. flow is expected origin-facility counts, while allocation is an inside probability operator. Requesting counts does not select a likelihood. utilization_by_group is the expected count of each group at each facility (a model with demand groups, see clm_allocation()). The group-specific parameters of such a model (sigma.<group>, v0.<group>, from by_group) can be fitted only to this output, with observed counts for every group that has one and positive demand in that group; aggregated targets leave them multimodal and weakly identified, so the fit is refused (before any start) with a message naming the parameters. Hold them (clm_allocation(fixed = ), or numbers in the decay and outside slots of spec_clm()), or fit shared parameters to any target. flow_outside, utilization_outside and utilization_outside_by_group are the three count outputs above with the modelled outside count added as one more column, element or row named "(outside)" (see the section on outside counts); they need a model with an outside option. The group-specific parameters can also be fitted to utilization_outside_by_group.

loss

"weighted_sse", "poisson", or a function accepting predicted and observed values. Weighted SSE divides squared residuals by observed+eta, with eta=1 by default. Poisson omits the data-only log-factorial constant. It floors modelled counts at eps (loss_args), 1e-250 by default, only to avoid the log of zero; cells with positive observed counts modelled below the floor are reported with a warning, because the loss is capped there. Fits made before this default used 1e-9; pass loss_args = list(eps = 1e-9) to reproduce them. Joint fitting does not force total matching. The default is "weighted_sse" when starts are given; without starts the loss must be named. The outside-count outputs accept "poisson" only (not the default weighted SSE and not a custom function).

loss_args

Named auxiliary arguments passed to loss callbacks. For loss = "poisson" an eps of 1e-250 is added when none is given; other arguments pass unchanged. Any observation-indexed values must already follow canonical observed order.

loss_grad

Optional matching parameter-gradient callback. Built-in choices supply their analytic loss gradients. A custom loss requires its own loss_grad when gradient=TRUE; none is invented.

gradient

Logical; use the implicit sensitivity route when TRUE. FALSE retains the underlying fitter's default behavior. When starts is NULL and gradient is not given, it is TRUE if the loss has a gradient (the built-in losses, or a custom loss with loss_grad).

...

Named multistart or fitting controls, including solver tolerances, optimizer control, keep_fits and descriptive disagreement tolerances. When starts is NULL and control is not given it is list(maxit = 300, factr = 1e3, pgtol = 1e-2).

Value

An ae_multistart_fit, retaining selected fit, all per-start diagnostics, boundaries, warnings/errors and descriptive disagreement. A fit whose starts came from the default search also has a default_search element: the rule, the sigma range, the number of grid points and of finite ones, the grid of sigma, v0 and loss, the starts, the bounds, the controls and the loss.

Details

A model whose decay kernel was declared with smooth = FALSE (see decay_kernel()) is refused, because fitting needs a kernel that is smooth in sigma. Evaluate such a kernel at fixed parameters with evaluate_allocation(), for example over a grid of sigma and v0.

Outside counts. The outputs flow_outside, utilization_outside and utilization_outside_by_group are flow, utilization and utilization_by_group with the modelled outside count added: the demand of the active origins that goes to the outside option, that is, to facilities that are not in the data or to none. For flow_outside the outside count of origin i is D_i * outside_share_i, one more column (each row then adds up to the demand of the origin); utilization_outside adds the sum of these over the origins as one more element, and utilization_outside_by_group adds, for each group, the sum of its demand times its outside share as one more row. They are available for a model with an outside option (a fitted v0, or a held v0 above 0) and are refused as targets for any other model, such as the Huff model: "outside counts need a model with an outside option". They are fitted like the other count outputs, with the built-in Poisson loss (loss = "poisson") and no further argument; any other loss, the default weighted SSE and custom loss functions included, is refused: "outside counts are fitted with loss = \"poisson\"". The observed counts carry the outside counts under the name "(outside)": a column of the flow matrix, an element of the totals vector, a row of the facility-by-group matrix, matched by name like the facility IDs and in any order. NA is allowed: an origin or group whose outside count is not known carries no outside term, and its facility counts are used as before. A facility cannot have the ID "(outside)".

What an outside count means depends on how the counts were recorded. It is the demand of the data's active origins that went to facilities outside the data or to none, so for flows it is known by subtraction, y0_i = D_i - sum_j y_ij, only when demand counts the same people as the observations (for example registrations by residence from the same extract and date). It is not a population estimate: list sizes and population differ by several percent, and the gap goes straight into the outside count. For an origin whose outside count is known and y0_i + sum_j y_ij = D_i, the Poisson loss on its cells (facilities and outside) is the multinomial likelihood of its choices up to constants. When this holds for every origin of a flow fit and v0 is free and inside its bounds, the fitted model's total outside count equals the observed one (the score equation of log v0). This is not claimed for totals or for models with demand groups: there the total outside count is not guaranteed to match. Fits to different outputs, or with and without outside counts, are fits to different data, so compare_allocations() gives no loss difference between them; compare models on the same observation, and a model without an outside option (Huff) on the observation without outside counts. bootstrap_allocation() refuses these fits: the facility-case bootstrap is defined for facility totals without outside counts.

Default search. For the count outputs starts, lower and upper are optional. When starts is NULL they come from the data (loss must then be named, because the estimator is not chosen silently):

  1. the decay kernel is probed at the nearest, a far and the largest travel time of the data for the range of sigma over which it still decays over the travel times, whatever the unit of the travel times;

  2. sigma takes 15 log-spaced values over that range, from the steepest to the flattest kernel (group-specific sigmas walk together);

  3. a fitted outside weight v0 is seeded from the observed outside share, times 0.1, 1 and 10, and a fitted beta starts at 1 (for the outside-count outputs the seed reads the facility counts only, the "(outside)" entries dropped, as for flow and utilization);

  4. the loss is evaluated at every point, by the code the fit itself uses;

  5. the fit starts from the best point of up to three sigma values (local minima along the grid first), named scan1, scan2, ...

The default bounds are the probed range for sigma; for v0, from a thousandth of the smallest to a thousand times the largest of the best values on the grid; and 0.05 to 5 for beta. Bounds you give replace the default ones one by one, and starts you give widen the default bounds to include them (the scan then runs only to find a default bound of v0). The search is recorded in the default_search element of the result.

When the starts come from the search, gradient and control default (each unless you give it) to analytic gradients, when the loss has one, and strict optimizer settings, control = list(maxit = 300, factr = 1e3, pgtol = 1e-2), because the optimizer defaults can stop early at a different outside weight. Given starts keep the earlier defaults.

A model in which every sigma is held (demand groups with fixed) has no sigma to probe or scan: the starts are the three v0 seeds at the held values, or, with only beta free, beta = 0.5, 1 and 2.

A fully observed target whose counts reach the total demand has no outside share for v0 to explain: the search stops with an error (use no outside option: fit_v0 = FALSE), and warns when the counts are within 0.1% of the total demand (for the outside-count outputs these are the facility counts, without the "(outside)" entries). Starts and bounds remain required for any output other than utilization, flow, utilization_by_group and the three outside-count outputs, and calls that give starts, lower and upper run exactly as before.

The cost is about one solve of the model per grid point, 15 to 45 solves: about a second on the 336 by 54 Cornwall example, about 24 seconds for 20,000 origins and 400 facilities, which is roughly the cost of one strict start. Give your own starts to skip it.

See also

allocation-fit-methods for methods on saved fits.

Other allocation steps: bootstrap_fit(), calc_demand(), calc_travel_time(), check_fit(), clm_allocation(), compare_fits(), decay_kernel(), evaluate_allocation(), huff_allocation(), predict_allocation(), prepare_allocation()

Examples

# West Cornwall: the small areas and practices west of easting 170 km
areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa)
areas <- areas[!areas$scilly & areas$cent_x < 170000, ]
gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp)
gp <- gp[!gp$scilly & gp$easting < 170000, ]
travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice]
inputs <- prepare_allocation(stats::setNames(areas$registered, areas$lsoa),
                             stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice),
                             travel)
model <- clm_allocation(inputs, fit_v0 = TRUE)

# Registrations of these residents at these practices
flows <- cornwall_flows[cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% areas$lsoa &
                          cornwall_flows$practice %in% gp$practice, ]

# Fit to the practice totals. Without starts, the search finds starts and
# bounds from the data, and the loss must be named
totals <- sapply(split(flows$patients, flows$practice), sum)
fit <- fit_allocation(model, totals, loss = "poisson")
fit
#> <allocation fit> 3 starts, selected scan1
#> eligible starts: 3 / 3
#> selected start: scan1
#> starts: default search, 45 of 45 grid points, loss poisson
#> loss disagreement: FALSE; parameter disagreement: FALSE
#>  start     loss eligible optim_convergence solver_converged residual seconds
#>  scan1 -1200843     TRUE                 0             TRUE        0   0.036
#>  scan2 -1200843     TRUE                 0             TRUE        0   0.060
#>  scan3 -1200843     TRUE                 0             TRUE        0   0.043
#>  boundary   status                                    optim_message
#>     FALSE eligible CONVERGENCE: NORM OF PROJECTED GRADIENT <= PGTOL
#>     FALSE eligible CONVERGENCE: NORM OF PROJECTED GRADIENT <= PGTOL
#>     FALSE eligible CONVERGENCE: NORM OF PROJECTED GRADIENT <= PGTOL
#>  solver_message log_parameter_gap     loss_gap
#>       converged      0.000000e+00 0.000000e+00
#>       converged      8.513597e-07 0.000000e+00
#>       converged      6.201278e-06 1.164153e-09
coef(fit)
#>     sigma        v0 
#> 13.223212  1.001842 

# Fit to the flows: a matrix of small areas by practices, 0 where none. Demand
# counts every registered resident, so the residents registered elsewhere are
# known: they are one more column, "(outside)", fitted by the outside option
flow_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow(travel), ncol(travel), dimnames = dimnames(travel))
flow_matrix[cbind(flows$lsoa, flows$practice)] <- flows$patients
flow_matrix <- cbind(flow_matrix, "(outside)" = areas$registered - rowSums(flow_matrix))
coef(fit_allocation(model, flow_matrix, output = "flow_outside", loss = "poisson"))
#>      sigma         v0 
#> 3.97012750 0.09627051 

# Starts and bounds of your own: one start per row
starts <- rbind(near = c(sigma = 5, v0 = 0.5), far = c(sigma = 30, v0 = 5))
fit_own <- fit_allocation(model, totals, starts = starts,
                          lower = c(sigma = 1, v0 = 0.001),
                          upper = c(sigma = 100, v0 = 100), loss = "poisson")
coef(fit_own)
#>     sigma        v0 
#> 13.223190  1.001846
